Pellucid

/puh-LOO-sid/ - the stress falls on LOO · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pellucid means crystal clear and easy to understand.

The coach's pellucid chalk talk turned a trick play into three arrows anyone could follow.

Worked Example

The tax office rewrote its dreaded Form 61 last year, and the difference startled people. The old instructions sent filers three paragraphs backward for every defined term; the new ones walk down the page in short declarative steps, one idea to a sentence, and a first-time filer finishes in twenty minutes without phoning anyone. Complaints to the help desk fell by half before the season ended.

Pellucid is the exact word for the rewrite, because pellucid means crystal clear and easy to understand — prose you see straight through to the meaning, the way you see a stream's pebbles through still water. Simple can mean dumbed down, something removed; pellucid keeps the full idea and loses only the fog around it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

crystal-clear: the everyday compound for the same see-through quality

clear as glass: the simile pellucid compresses into a single word

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

murky: hard to see into; meaning lost in silt

impenetrable: no light gets through at all

Where it sits · how effortlessly the meaning comes through — readable → clear → pellucid

readable vs. pellucid: Readable clears the lowest bar — you can get through it without getting lost.

clear vs. pellucid: Clear stops short of pellucid — clear writing is easily followed; pellucid writing seems to vanish, leaving only the idea shining in place.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pel-

Prefix — pel-: through (Latin per-, assimilated)

Root — luc

Root — luc: light (Latin lux, lucere, to shine)

Suffix — -id

Suffix — -id: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Pel- (through) + luc (light) + -id (having the quality of) = letting light pass through. Latin pellucidus described water and crystal the eye passes through; English kept the glass and added prose — pellucid writing is the sentence light passes through with nothing scattered.

Use the root in a new word: translucent

Use the root in a new word: translucent: Trans- means through as well, so a translucent curtain lets the morning light pass — the same luc- glowing in both words.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Pellucid is a reviewer's word — praise for proofs, prose, and explanations, always with the picture of light passing through. Clear is the workhorse; crystal-clear the everyday superlative; lucid, its close Latin cousin, leans toward a mind staying clear. Patent, its unit-mate, is a different clarity: a patent fact is obvious whether or not anyone explains it, while pellucid praises the explaining itself.
